title: Vice-President hails DNHDD as a “Mini India”, appreciates transformative development under PM Narendra Modi and Administrator Praful Patel
subtitle:
DNHDD emerging as a model of people-centric development with active participation of people: Vice-President

“DNHDD’s transformation is contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047”: Vice-President

Healthcare, education, tourism and connectivity driving transformation in the Union Territory: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed a public function at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Government College, Silvassa, during his maiden visit to the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed a public function at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Government College, Silvassa today, during his maiden visit to the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

The Vice-President said that the Union Territory is a remarkable example of how innovative governance and people’s participation can drive transformative development.

The Vice-President appreciated the Union Territory’s social diversity, cultural heritage and spirit of harmony and described it as a “mini India”. He said that people from different parts of the country are contributing to the region’s growth and living together in harmony.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 11, 2026
On the occasion, the Vice-President was felicitated by public representatives, including Hon’ble Administrator Shri Praful Patel and Hon’ble Member of Parliament Smt. Kalaben Mohanbhai Delkar, along with representatives of District Panchayats, Municipal Councils, industry and hotel associations, topper students from various colleges and the Tamil Sangam. He also distributed toolkits to PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries and appointment certificates to newly appointed teachers.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the Union Territory is a remarkable example of how innovative governance and people’s participation can drive transformative development. He appreciated the progress achieved over the last decade under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the sustained efforts of Administrator Shri Praful Patel, with active participation of the people.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that over 450 infrastructure projects worth more than ₹13,000 crore have been undertaken in the Union Territory during the last decade, including around 800 km of roads at a cost of over ₹4,000 crore.
Highlighting the transformation in healthcare, he noted that the Union Territory, which did not have a medical college before 2019, now has one with 177 seats, besides the 450-bed NAMO Hospital in Silvassa and the recently inaugurated 350-bed NAMO Hospital in Daman. TB cases have declined by 57 per cent and malnutrition by 58 per cent over the last three years. The Union Territory has also achieved 100 per cent saturation of Health and Wellness Centres and institutional deliveries, along with full registration under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.
On education, the Vice-President highlighted the construction of 21 new schools at an investment of over ₹700 crore, with 16 more under construction, besides smart classrooms in government schools. He also noted the establishment of institutions and campuses of NIFT, Gujarat National Law University and other professional institutions, expanding opportunities for the youth within the Union Territory.
Highlighting the growing importance of tourism, the Vice-President noted that tourist footfall has increased from around 6 lakh in 2021 to nearly 50 lakh in 2025. He said that initiatives such as the Daman Night Market, Ram-setu Seafront, restored heritage sites, beaches, water sports and eco-tourism projects are creating new opportunities while showcasing the region’s rich heritage and natural beauty.
The Vice-President also highlighted the Union Territory’s industrial strength, with more than 7,500 manufacturing units and over 2.8 lakh employment opportunities through the MSME sector. The inauguration of Namo Airport, Daman has further strengthened air connectivity with Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad. He also appreciated the Union Territory for achieving 100 per cent solarisation of government buildings, with nearly 12 MW of installed capacity.
Referring to the contributions of Gujarat’s three iconic leaders, Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that Gandhi represents non-violence and the freedom struggle, Sardar Patel symbolises the unity and integrity of India, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi represents development.
The Vice-President said that the Union Territory’s social diversity, cultural heritage and spirit of harmony make it a “mini India”. He said that people from different parts of the country are contributing to the region’s growth and living together in harmony.

title: English Translation of Prime Minister’s Address at the BRICS Business Forum 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Excellencies
Leaders of the BRICS business community,
Innovators and friends,
Namaskar!
A warm welcome to all of you to the BRICS Business Forum.
This year, we are celebrating twenty years of BRICS. When the group was launched in 2006, it comprised only four countries. Today, including BRICS and its partners, we have a family of twenty-one countries.
Today, the BRICS countries represent 50% of the world’s population, 40% of global GDP, and more than 25% of global trade. Not only that, over these years, while global GDP has grown by around 2.5 times, the combined GDP of BRICS countries has grown by around 4.5 times. In other words, the economic strength of BRICS has grown at nearly twice the pace of the world economy.
BRICS countries are also emerging as important centres for global innovation and solutions. From grassroots initiatives to frontier technologies, new possibilities for innovation are taking shape across our countries. The growing scale, speed, and optimism of BRICS are clearly visible among us. The Forum being held in India is the largest-ever BRICS Business Forum.
Friends,
The theme of India’s BRICS Presidency is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
Over the past twelve years, India has made this mantra the foundation of its economic and trade policy. When it comes to resilience, India has made its supply chains more diversified and reliable, from energy to technology. It is this very resilience that has enabled India, even amid global uncertainties, to offer the world confidence in growth and stability.
We are rapidly expanding our roads, railways, ports, and airports. At the same time, we are building new capabilities in strategic sectors such as shipbuilding, semiconductors, quantum technology, critical minerals, and biotechnology. In these sectors, India is emerging as a hub of new opportunities for global businesses. Therefore, Make in India, Innovate with India, and Scale for the World.
Friends,
Today, India is witnessing a start-up revolution. With more than 200,000 start-ups and over 120 unicorns, India is emerging as a hub for global solutions. You will get a glimpse of this at the BRICS Bharat Innovates Expo.
Our start-ups are transforming education and healthcare through AI, working on Green Hydrogen and Batteries, and breaking new frontiers in defence and space. Now, through BRICS as well, we must take these world-class innovations to global markets.
Friends,
Another distinctive feature of India’s innovation story is Innovation at Population Scale. India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has given new momentum to financial inclusion and digital transactions at population scale.
Today, 50% of the world’s real-time payments are powered by this technology. To build new solutions on this digital layer, we have provided industry and start-ups with an open ecosystem. We are proud that many countries are adopting India’s world-class ecosystem. Innovators from BRICS countries can also draw on this experience to develop new solutions for their own countries.
Friends,
Today, as trade barriers are increasing around the world, India is building economic bridges. Since 2014, we have entered into Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries around the world. Our approach within BRICS is also the same, reduce barriers and expand opportunities for businesses.
Therefore, under our Presidency, we have established new cooperation networks in areas such as agriculture, healthcare, skills, and smart grids. To connect start-ups and SMEs with markets and finance, we have launched initiatives such as the BRICS Incubator Network, BRICS MSME Portal, and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund.
You can all benefit from these cooperation frameworks and further increase the exchange of investment and talent among our countries.
Friends,
Global trade can move forward only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes remain open, and seafarers are safe. That is why India is a staunch advocate of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers.
The BRICS Women’s Business Alliance is also an important part of our vision. We want women entrepreneurs to lead our growth story. We are very pleased that nearly 200 women business leaders participated in the meeting of this Alliance held in India.
Friends,
As BRICS enters its third decade, I would urge the BRICS Business Council to consider … can you prepare a report on removing the top 10 trade barriers among BRICS countries? Can we support 100 BRICS startups every year to scale into other BRICS markets? Can we develop 1,000 new partnerships among our businesses? We should review our progress every year against these three benchmarks.
Let us transform BRICS’ ambition into action and our collective strength into global solutions. May BRICS move forward and help the world move forward as well.
Thank you all very much.

title: Prime Minister meets with the President of the Russian Federation on the sidelines of BRICS Summit
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today met with the President of the Russian Federation, H.E. Vladimir Putin, on the margins of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. This was their second meeting this year. The two leaders had met earlier in Bishkek on the sidelines of the 26th SCO Summit on 31st August 2026.
The two leaders reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation in political, economic, defence, energy, space, skill mobility and people-to- people domains. They welcomed Russia’s International Industrial Exhibition "INNOPROM India", which was held for the first time in India from 9-11 September 2026 and underscored its importance in further expanding trade and industrial ties. The two leaders also visited the INNOPROM India exhibition and interacted with the participants.
The leaders exchanged views on India-Russia engagement in the multilateral sphere, in particular in BRICS under India’s Chairship for 2026. They also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. Prime Minister once again reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts and India stood ready to assist in peace efforts.
The two leaders agreed to remain engaged in an effort to strengthen further the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries, which continues to register significant growth and has shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties.
President Putin invited Prime Minister to visit Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit. Prime Minister accepted the invitation. The dates of the Summit will be decided as per mutual convenience through diplomatic channels.

title: NITI Aayog Member (Health) Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas Visits CCRAS-NIIMH, Hyderabad
subtitle: Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas Calls for Global Standards and Greater Visibility of India’s Medical Heritage
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, Government of India, visited the CCRAS–National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), Ministry of Ayush, Hyderabad. He was accompanied by Dr. Shobhit Kumar, OSD (Health), NITI Aayog, and Dr. Janvi Prajapati, Young Professional, NITI Aayog.
Dr. N. Srikanth, Deputy Director General, Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), New Delhi, welcomed Prof. Srinivas and briefed him on the institute’s initiatives, digital portals, repositories and historical research in traditional systems of medicine. He also emphasised the strategic role of NIIMH in documenting and preserving India’s rich medical heritage. Dr. Goli Penchala Prasad, Assistant Director In-charge, NIIMH, gave an overview of the institute’s activities, key milestones and achievements.
During the visit, Prof. Srinivas visited the museum, library and research divisions and interacted with officers and project staff. He also viewed a documentary on Agalya and the Rani Rudramadevi inscription, developed by the institute under the SAHI project.
Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas, in his address, commended the efforts of CCRAS–NIIMH in digitising rare manuscripts, maintaining historical scientific records and strengthening the preservation of India’s medical heritage through advanced information systems and research portals.
Prof. Srinivas called for adoption of international practices and standards for the preservation and maintenance of the museum. He also stressed the importance of introducing training courses, certificate courses and collaborative joint post-doctoral programmes to build capacity and develop skilled manpower for the preservation of India’s rich medical heritage.
Prof. Srinivas also suggested positioning NIIMH as a destination for educational tourism for students and professionals from medical and allied disciplines. He emphasised the need to enhance the institute’s visibility and global recognition.
He further recommended that NIIMH engage with regulatory bodies such as the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Medical Commission (NMC) to connect with students and faculty. He also suggested developing mini-museums at IITs and other Institutions of National Importance to facilitate wider dissemination of India’s rich medical heritage.
Prof. Srinivas appreciated the efforts of the institute towards preserving India’s rich medical heritage and assured support for further strengthening its activities. In the visitors’ book, he described NIIMH as a “Temple” preserving India’s rich medical history and appreciated the dedication of its leadership and staff towards protecting and preserving the heritage for future generations.

title: "Students of today are the Torchbearers of Tomorrow's Democracy": CEC Gyanesh Kumar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised its fifth regional conference on "Electoral Literacy Clubs and ECINET" in Ahmedabad today, focusing on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens. Addressing the gathering, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar said that the students of today are the torchbearers of tomorrow’s democracy. He added that Electoral Literacy Clubs across India will help strengthen the backbone of the world's oldest and largest democracy.
The earlier regional conferences on "Electoral Literacy Clubs and ECINET" were held at Patna (Bihar), Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh), Chennai (Tamil Nadu) and Margao (Goa).
Addressing the participants comprising students and teachers from schools, colleges and universities across Gujarat, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar described students as the future of the nation, stating that ELCs are imperative in carrying forth the understanding of electoral processes and enriching democracy. He further emphasised that engaging young citizens and securing their trust and informed participation in the electoral process is an investment in the future of democracy.
He underlined the need for students and young electors to familiarise themselves with India’s electoral system, democratic values, electoral registration, polling and counting processes, and the role and functioning of the Election Commission of India.
CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated that elections in India are held strictly as per the Constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and are conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages.
ELC 2.0, with the tagline "Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.", reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally-enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities, encouraging young and first-time voters to understand and meaningfully participate in democracy. Leveraging the extensive ECINET digital platform, which provides all election-related services from roll to poll, the initiative will drive continuous, year-round electoral literacy activities through a dedicated ELC portal, building a streamlined pan-India network of ELCs.
The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students.
Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation. The ELCs will also disseminate information on electoral registration, polling, counting, ECINET App and other key ECI initiatives.
Earlier in the day, in an interactive session with over 500 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) of Gujarat, CEC Gyanesh Kumar congratulated the BLOs for their service which resulted in smooth execution of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls in the State.
The students and the BLOs had a Question-and-Answer session with the CEC as part of the meeting. BLOs had an opportunity to clarify their doubts directly through the interaction.

title: 50 Years of ICAR–ICRISAT Partnership Celebrated at Dryland Congress 2026
subtitle: Experts Deliberate on Resilient Farming Systems, Seed Systems, Gender and Youth-Centred Transformation
date:

content:
The second day of Dryland Congress 2026 in New Delhi today featured a special session commemorating 50 years of collaboration between the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT). The session brought together former and current leaders of both institutions to reflect on five decades of partnership and deliberate on a roadmap for strengthening collaboration and accelerating agricultural transformation towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
The special session was co-chaired by Dr R. S. Paroda, Former Director General, ICAR, and Dr William D. Dar, Former Director General, ICRISAT. Former leaders of ICAR and ICRISAT, including Dr Panjab Singh, Former Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR; Dr C. L. L. Gowda, Former Deputy Director General, ICRISAT; Dr T. R. Sharma, Former Deputy Director General, Crop Science, ICAR; and Dr Swapan Datta, Former Deputy Director General, Crop Science, ICAR, shared their reflections on the evolution and achievements of the partnership.
Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, provided a strategic outlook for the partnership and emphasised the need to leverage the complementary strengths of ICAR and ICRISAT to address emerging agricultural challenges and create greater impact. Yadava, Deputy Director General, Crop Science, ICAR, and Dr Raman Babu, Global Research Program Director, Accelerated Crop Improvement, ICRISAT, presented a roadmap for strengthening ICAR–ICRISAT collaboration towards Viksit Bharat 2047, with emphasis on leveraging scientific capabilities and translating research into greater impact.

These deliberations were complemented by parallel technical sessions covering resilient dryland farming systems, seed systems in the Global South, and gender- and youth-centred transformation. The sessions brought together researchers, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to discuss approaches for strengthening resilience, improving access to agricultural innovations and ensuring greater participation of women and young people in dryland agriculture.

Dr Panjab Singh highlighted the significant outcomes achieved through the ICAR–ICRISAT partnership over the past five decades and stressed that the next phase should focus on scaling successful models and ensuring that innovations reach farmers on a larger scale.
Dr William D. Dar emphasised that the future of dryland agriculture would depend on combining scientific capabilities with strong partnerships, innovation and scale, with greater focus on income security, nutrition security and resilience of farming communities.
On gender and youth-centred transformation, Prof. Yaye Gassama, ICRISAT Board Member, emphasised the importance of greater participation of women and young people in shaping solutions for dryland regions through leadership, innovation and enterprise.

title: Monsoon Resilience: Captive Mines Delivering Growth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Captive mines have been a mainstay of coal production, and their output has grown steadily. Production from captive mines rose from 167.44 MT in FY 2024-25 to 184 MT in FY 2025-26, a growth of 10.10%. Along with commercial mines, which produced ~26 MT, the captive and commercial segment together accounted for 210 MT in FY 2025-26 against 190.95 MT the previous year. Captive and Commercial mines account for about 21% of total domestic coal production, which stood at 1,039 MT in FY 2025-26 and has remained above one billion tonnes for the second year running.
The performance has carried into the current year. Captive mines produced 68.98 MT up to 10 September 2026, against 65.78 MT in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26. This is a growth of about 5%, or an additional 3.2 MT, and it comes on a base that was itself 10.12% higher than the year before it. The gain has been recorded in the first five months of the year, which include the monsoon, when mining and evacuation are at their most difficult. Dispatch from captive mines has also been better than previous year. Captive mines dispatched 75.68 MT against 71.43 MT last year, a growth of 5.94% and an increase of 4.25 MT.
Provisional figures indicate the pace picking up further as the monsoon begins to recede. In the ten days between 01 September and 10 September 2026, captive mines produced 4.12 MT and dispatched 4.21 MT.
New capacity is being added steadily to this base. Nine captive & commercial mines are expected to commence production during FY 2026-27, with a combined peak rated capacity of 20.67 MT. Three of these, with peak capacity of 7.51 MT, have already started production during the current year. The remaining six, are expected to commence production soon during the year.
On this footing, production from captive mines is expected to cross 190 MT in FY 2026-27. Together with commercial mines, the two segments are expected to exceed 228 MT during the current financial year.

title: Facts on Auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 12:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Recently, reports have appeared in media on the auction of the Tara Coal block. These reports are misleading and incomplete facts have been used in these reports. These reports do not take into account the important developments that took place after 2023, which ultimately led to the auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block in 2026.
It is a fact that the Tara coal block offered under the 7th Tranche in 2023 was taken out of commercial coal mine auctions as letter was received from Government of Chhattisgarh for the exclusion of coal blocks in Hasdeo Arand area from the commercial coal mine auctions.
Accordingly, the coal blocks in Hasdeo Arand area having overlap with Lemru elephant corridor were not offered in the subsequent tranches of commercial coal mine auctions.
However, a letter dated 11.12.2025 was received from Government of Chhattisgarh to include the Tara coal block stating that “
the coal block is outside the Lemru Elephant Corridor, and the coal block may be offered in the upcoming tranche of auction
”.
Accordingly, the coal block was put up for auction under the 15th round of commercial coal mine auction duly removing the influence zone of Lemru Elephant Corridor and has been successfully auctioned.
It is pertinent to mention that the coal block has gathered a lot of interest from the market. A total of 9 bids were received for the coal block under the 15th round. The Block has been auctioned at a revenue share of 37.50%. The Coal Block is expected to generate annual revenue of more than Rs 1200 crores to the state and generate employment for more than 8000 people.
It is clear from above that Tara Coal Block was excluded from auction in July 2023 after considering the concerns raised by the Government of Chhattisgarh. It was considered for auction again only after the State Government’s communication dated 11.12.2025 and after revision of the block boundary by CMPDIL. Therefore, the reports do not present the complete facts and overlooks important developments that led to the auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block.

title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Deeper, Resilient and More Balanced Intra-BRICS Trade
subtitle:
Shri Goyal Urges Member Countries to Open Markets and Simplify Regulatory Procedures

Shri Goyal Urges BRICS Member And Partner Countries to Link Payment Systems And Promote Trade in Each Other’s Local Currencies

Shri Goyal Emphasises Greater Cooperation in Agriculture, Pharmaceuticals, Engineering, Electronics, Automobiles, Services, Startups and Emerging Technologies

Union Minister of External Affairs Dr. S. Jaishankar Highlights Supply Chain Connectivity, Trade Facilitation and Innovation as Key BRICS Priorities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 12:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
With BRICS accounting for nearly one-fourth of global trade, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today underlined the need for member and partner countries to build deeper, more resilient and balanced trade partnerships. Addressing the Opening Session of the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi, Shri Goyal emphasised greater market access, diversified supply chains and simpler regulatory procedures to unlock the full potential of economic cooperation. He expressed hope that the Forum would deliver significant outcomes and take economic dialogue and business partnerships among BRICS countries to the next level.
The Opening Session was also addressed by H.E. Maxim Reshetnikov, Minister of Economic Development of the Russian Federation; Union Minister of External Affairs Dr. S. Jaishankar; Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce & Industry and Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada; and Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal.
Shri Goyal said India is an important pillar of intra-BRICS trade and highlighted the country’s strong capabilities in engineering goods and electronics, which account for the largest segment of India’s manufactured exports. He also noted that India is known as the pharmacy of the world. He said India sees BRICS as an important market for these and other products that it seeks to take to the world as a trusted partner.
Emphasising the importance of deep and resilient trade among partners, Shri Goyal said supply chains must be diversified and trade should not become an impediment to growth and the well-being of people in any member state. He called upon BRICS countries to open their markets for each other’s products, including raw materials and critical minerals.
Shri Goyal said supply chains would be resilient when they run both ways. Noting that non-tariff measures impose higher export costs than tariffs themselves for 88 per cent of countries, he called for easier and smoother market access. He urged BRICS member and partner countries to open their markets while working together to simplify regulatory procedures and facilitate faster clearance of consignments.
Calling for greater cooperation in agriculture, Shri Goyal urged BRICS countries to encourage agri-tech startups to jointly develop solutions for farmers across BRICS nations in the interest of food security. He also called upon countries to open their services markets to each other in a real sense, facilitate the movement of professionals across borders and make it easier to recognise each other’s professional qualifications.
Highlighting women’s participation in India’s startup and entrepreneurship ecosystem, Shri Goyal said that more than 45 per cent of the 250,000 recognised startups in India have at least one woman partner or director. He said two-thirds of the small loans provided in the last decade have been given to women entrepreneurs, helping them stand on their own feet and become independent and self-reliant. Referring to the meeting of the BRICS Women’s Business Alliance in New Delhi earlier in the week, he said he had urged the Alliance to ensure that women-led enterprises participate in every BRICS exhibition, trade fair and other opportunities that could be encouraged and supported.
Shri Goyal highlighted India’s significant initiatives in laying out digital public infrastructure and said that the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) today has over 250 billion transactions a year, representing more than half of transactions by volume across the world. He said UPI is also accepted in 11 countries and urged BRICS member and partner countries to link their payment systems, promote trade in each other’s local currencies, make digital trade global and build together for emerging technologies.
He said India brings strong capabilities across sectors including agriculture, pharmaceuticals, engineering, electronics, automobiles and auto components and services, and called for linking startup ecosystems as well. He said these trends offer significant scope for joint innovation, technology partnerships and resilient global value chains.
As India moves towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the collective goal that 1.4 billion Indians have set for themselves to make India a developed nation when the country celebrates 100 years of independence, Shri Goyal said there is immense potential to deepen cooperation with BRICS members and partner countries. He expressed hope that the thematic sessions would lead to constructive and actionable recommendations to further strengthen intra-BRICS trade and economic cooperation.
Union Minister of External Affairs Dr. S. Jaishankar in his address said that this year marks 20 years of institutionalised BRICS cooperation, during which BRICS has evolved substantially in membership, agenda and mechanisms of cooperation. He said India’s Chairship has sought to carry this evolution forward through the theme of resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. He said these priorities are especially relevant as the global political and economic order undergoes churn, with volatility, uncertainty and complexity becoming defining features, while geopolitical conflicts, pandemics, climate-related disruptions, digitisation and technological advances are reshaping the economic landscape.
Dr. Jaishankar said resilience has become a key component of the BRICS community, with the BRICS Business Council and BRICS Women’s Business Alliance playing an important role in bringing industry, entrepreneurs and business leaders into the BRICS process. He said supply chain connectivity and trade facilitation have emerged as crucial, alongside services, agriculture and agritechnology, digital delivery, MSMEs, startups and women-led enterprises. He stressed the need for greater self-reliance while remaining connected and competitive through genuine market practices, dependable logistics, a predictable business environment, diversified commercial relationships and transparent trade and investment. He also highlighted digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, fintech and advanced manufacturing as major opportunities, while noting questions of access, standards, security and trust.
Dr. Jaishankar said India’s Chairship has sought to strengthen the innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem through the BRICS incubator network and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund, stressing that the benefits must be accessible across the full spectrum of business communities. He said India’s experience makes it a natural partner, with a large and growing market, expanding manufacturing capabilities, deeper pools of talent, digital experience and a dynamic innovation and entrepreneurial base. As BRICS leaders prepare to meet, he said the Forum’s most useful contribution would be to bring a clear business perspective to the next phase of BRICS cooperation, focusing on opportunities, challenges faced by businesses and what governments can do to address them.
Speaking at the Opening session Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce & Industry and Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted that BRICS Business Forum provides an opportunity to convert the strength of BRICS economies into concrete commercial results. He highlighted digital services, particularly artificial intelligence, as an important area of collaboration, noting its potential to improve productivity, standard of living, incomes and outcomes for individuals and MSMEs, while ensuring access to compute, particularly in the Global South.
Shri Prasada stressed the need for greater technology exchange and cooperation in AI while keeping the United Nations at the centre of governance. On semiconductors, he highlighted India’s Semiconductor Mission 2.0 with a financial outlay of about USD 13 billion in incentives and called for collaboration to develop the entire semiconductor ecosystem.
He also highlighted Digital Public Infrastructure and data centres as areas of cooperation, including sharing India’s best practices, and called for BRICS countries to co-develop, co-invest and co-innovate, with greater resources for research and development and startups to enable young people to access markets across international borders.
Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal said that BRICS represents a significant and growing market, with trade among BRICS countries rising from USD 84 billion in 2003 to nearly USD 1.2 trillion in 2024.
He emphasised preserving and revitalising the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core and supporting MSMEs through affordable working capital, with the Jaipur Consensus providing a foundation for exploring a common BRICS mechanism.
Shri Agrawal highlighted strengthening global value chains through BRICS Connect, B2B partnerships, an annual BRICS Trade and Investment Expo, digital trade documentation and greater sectoral cooperation, including healthcare. He called for stronger economic integration just under the BRICS Economic Partnership Strategy 2030 through cooperation, trust, innovation and shared prosperity. Concluding his statement, Shri Agrawal wished the BRICS Business Forum every success.

title: India’s Coastline Must be Viewed as an Integrated Space of Ecology, Security, Economy, Technology and Human Development: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Coastal Ecology and Security Cannot be Addressed in Isolation; Need Holistic Coastal India Approach: Dr. Jitendra Singh

India’s 11,000–12,000 Km Long Coastline Offers Significant Potential for Marine Resources and 'Blue Economy'

Ocean Observation, Surveillance, Communication, Remote Sensing and Emerging Technologies Can Strengthen Coastal Security

Deep Ocean Mission and Indigenous Technologies Opening New Frontiers for Exploration of Marine Resources: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:

                11 SEP 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s coastline must be viewed as an interconnected space of ecology, security, economy, technology and human development, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said today while virtually addressing the National Conference on Coastal Ecology, Security and Sustainability (CCESS) 2026. India’s 11,000–12,000 km long coastline offers significant potential for marine resources and the "Blue Economy", he added.
The Minister said that the country's long coastline and extensive marine ecosystem offer significant opportunities, while also requiring an integrated approach combining scientific knowledge, environmental sustainability, security and economic development.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India has an 11,000–12,000 km long coastal area, among the longest in the world, and emphasised the importance of the ocean and coastal regions in the country's future development. He said that India's historical association with the ocean also reflects the knowledge and understanding of the marine environment possessed by its ancestors.
Highlighting the importance of the Deep Ocean Mission, the Minister said that India is moving towards exploring the largely unexplored resources of the deep ocean while simultaneously building indigenous capabilities. He noted that a totally indigenous research vessel, ORV Sagar Manthan, was launched recently, reflecting efforts towards self-reliance in deep-ocean research and exploration.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that robots and submersibles are being developed to explore the depths of the ocean. He also referred to the efforts to enhance India's capability for deep-sea exploration and said that the country's progress in this area would open up new possibilities for understanding and utilising marine resources.
The Minister linked deep-ocean exploration with India's emerging economic opportunities, saying that if the country is to take its economy to the next level, it will have to look towards resources that have not yet been fully explored. He identified marine and coastal resources, including metals, minerals and fisheries, as areas with significant potential.
Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the potential of marine resources to contribute to the country's economic development while ensuring environmental sustainability. Referring to research on black sulphite and minerals, he said that the possibility of extracting marine minerals in the future represents one of the areas being explored. He also highlighted work aimed at increasing the economic potential of fisheries.
The Minister emphasised that coastal communities are an integral part of the wider coastal ecosystem. He said that efforts to expand the economic potential of coastal resources must also focus on improving the livelihoods of communities living along the coast while ensuring protection of the environment.
Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the growing technological dimension of coastal security. He said that ocean observation, surveillance, communication, remote sensing, data and emerging technologies can play an important role in strengthening India's understanding of and preparedness for the coastal and marine environment.
The Minister said that these technological capabilities need to be brought together through a holistic Coastal India approach, with the combined participation of the Government and the wider nation. He emphasised that the challenges and opportunities associated with the coastline cannot be addressed by individual sectors working in isolation.
In this context, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the National Conference on Coastal Ecology, Security and Sustainability (CCESS) 2026 provides an important platform for bringing together different areas of expertise. The conference's multidisciplinary character, involving earth sciences, academia, defence, maritime institutions, legal experts, industry and coastal stakeholders, provides an opportunity to develop an integrated understanding of coastal challenges.
The Minister emphasised that coastal ecology and coastal security cannot be addressed in isolation. He said that resilient coastal regions require healthy marine ecosystems, informed communities, effective governance and strong scientific capabilities.
Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the importance of connecting ocean science with national policy, so that scientific knowledge can contribute directly to coastal planning and management. He also emphasised the role of coastal communities, noting that their livelihoods, traditional knowledge and participation are integral to sustainable coastal development.
He said that India's coastal infrastructure and ports are central to connectivity, trade and economic growth, and that sustainable development of these assets requires a sound scientific understanding of coastal and marine environments.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the "Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar" campaign, which has been undertaken for the past five years. He recalled that a 75-day campaign was launched in 2022 and involved participation from citizens and different stakeholders across coastal States.
The Minister said that the campaign would continue this year from 12 September to 19 September, with a range of activities including clean-up drives and participation of NGOs and organisations. He also highlighted the introduction of a pledge for keeping India's coastline clean, adding a citizen-participation component to the campaign.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the larger objective should be to develop a holistic Coastal Bharat approach in which environmental sustainability, economic opportunity, scientific capability and coastal security reinforce one another. He emphasised the need to move away from working in separate domains towards an integrated framework that can convert scientific knowledge into collaboration, research priorities and practical action for a secure, sustainable and prosperous coastal future.

, which received the assent of the President on

where the bank is not a party to the proceedings, with a
“special cause” to be recorded in writing by the Court
for such summoning.
Further, the
Central Government may extend the provisions to specified financial sector entities or classes of entities
, allowing the framework to cater to the evolving financial landscape.
These reforms reflect the Government’s continued commitment to modernising laws in line with technological advancements and evolving economic needs, promoting ease of doing business and strengthening a modern and efficient financial system.

title: Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) Organizes National Conference on Quality and Safety of Biosimilars: Strengthening India’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision
subtitle:
Conference Aligns with the Government’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision to Strengthen India’s Biopharmaceutical Ecosystem through Innovation, Self-Reliance, Quality and Global Competitiveness

IPC Launches Indian Pharmacopoeia Reference Substance (IPRS) for Enoxaparin Sodium for bioassays
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, organized a two-day National Conference on “Quality and Safety of Biosimilars: Strengthening India’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision” on September 10–11, 2026, at the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP), Bengaluru. The conference was attended by 160 participants from regulatory authorities, industry, academia, research organizations and other stakeholder groups.
The conference was organized by IPC in collaboration with the Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association (IDMA), with the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) and Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP) serving as Knowledge Partners, and the Karnataka Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Manufacturers’ Association (KDPMA) as the Associate Partner. The conference aligns with the Government of India’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision to strengthen India’s biopharmaceutical ecosystem through innovation, self-reliance, quality and global competitiveness.
The conference addressed key scientific and regulatory challenges associated with the development, evaluation and safety of biosimilars, with emphasis on pharmacopoeial standards, critical quality attributes, analytical characterization, comparability assessment, immunogenicity, pharmacovigilance and evolving regulatory expectations.
A major highlight of the conference was the release of the Indian Pharmacopoeia Reference Substance (IPRS) for Enoxaparin Sodium for bioassays. Enoxaparin Sodium is a low-molecular-weight heparin and anticoagulant widely used for the prevention and treatment of thromboembolic disorders. The IPRS for Enoxaparin Sodium for bioassays may serve as an authenticated reference material for bioassay testing, supporting accurate, consistent, and comparable assessment of its biological activity. The release of the IPRS marks an important advancement in strengthening the availability of authenticated pharmacopoeial reference substances for bioassay-related testing of Enoxaparin Sodium, while contributing to the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision by strengthening India’s indigenous pharmaceutical quality infrastructure.
The inaugural session was addressed by distinguished representatives from IPC, SLA-Karnataka, NIB, IDMA, C-CAMP, and BIRAC, who emphasized the importance of strengthening quality, safety, and regulatory confidence in biosimilars. The session also highlighted the need for sustained collaboration among regulatory authorities, pharmacopoeial institutions, industry, academia, and research organizations to support the development of a robust and globally competitive biopharmaceutical sector.
Addressing the participants, Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC, highlighted the importance of strengthening pharmacopoeial standards, reliable analytical evaluation, safety monitoring, and regulatory cooperation to ensure the quality and safety of biosimilars. He also emphasized the need to align Indian practices with evolving regulatory expectations, support biopharmaceutical innovation, and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Technical sessions featured experts from IPC, SLA, WHO, USP, NIB, IDMA, BIRAC, C-CAMP, and leading biopharmaceutical organizations, providing perspectives spanning pharmacopoeial standard-setting, regulatory science, analytical development, safety monitoring, and innovation in biologics.
A dedicated Panel Discussion on the first day of the conference brought together senior experts from regulatory authorities, the biopharmaceutical industry, and academia to examine measures required to strengthen India’s biosimilar ecosystem. title: India Administers 80 Lakh HPV Vaccine Doses, Marking Major Milestone in Cervical Cancer Prevention
subtitle:
More than 8 Million HPV Vaccine Doses Administered Under National HPV Vaccination Campaign

Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram Achieve 100% Coverage; Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam Cross 90%

Uttar Pradesh Leads with More than 22 Lakh Adolescent Girls Vaccinated

All Vaccination Sessions Conducted Under Medical Supervision with 24×7 Arrangements for Management of Rare AEFI

National HPV Vaccination Campaign Launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2026 to Provide Free, Voluntary Single-Dose Vaccination to 14-Year-Old Girls
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India has crossed a significant milestone in its efforts to prevent cervical cancer, with more than
80 lakh (8 million) doses of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine administered
under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign since its launch in February 2026. The milestone marks the expanding reach of HPV vaccination through the public health system and reinforces India’s commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare for adolescent girls.
The National HPV Vaccination Campaign was
launched by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in February 2026
. Under the campaign,
14-year-old girls are provided voluntary and free-of-cost single-dose HPV vaccination, with parental consent, at Government health facilities
.
As per Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 estimates, approximately
1.2 crore girls constitute the annual cohort of 14-year-olds
who are expected to benefit from the initiative each year.
States and Union Territories have made significant progress in expanding HPV vaccination coverage, with several States achieving complete coverage of their identified target cohorts.
Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram have achieved 100 per cent coverage
of their respective identified target populations.
Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam have crossed 90 per cent coverage
, while
Karnataka has achieved more than 85 per cent coverage
.
Chhattisgarh, Sikkim, Kerala, Telangana and Odisha have crossed 60 per cent coverage
.
Among States,
Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest number of vaccinations, with more than 22 lakh adolescent girls vaccinated
under the campaign.
The progress reflects coordinated implementation by States and Union Territories, sustained community mobilisation and active engagement of district-level health teams. States have adopted context-specific approaches to reach eligible adolescent girls through the public health delivery network, including in rural, urban, remote and geographically challenging areas.
Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat have achieved 100 per cent coverage of their identified target cohorts
, supported by sustained community mobilisation, coordinated implementation and focused field-level efforts. The progress in
Assam and other Northeastern States
also demonstrates the role of integrated community health networks and coordinated field-level action in expanding access across geographically diverse areas.
The campaign has placed strong emphasis on
community engagement and credible information
, with parents, healthcare providers, teachers and frontline health workers being actively engaged to address concerns and counter misinformation relating to HPV vaccination.
Healthcare providers, including paediatricians, gynaecologists and experts from institutions such as AIIMS, along with teachers and frontline health workers including ASHAs and ANMs, have supported awareness and mobilisation efforts across States and districts.
The campaign has also leveraged
India’s digital health infrastructure through the U-WIN platform
, enabling programme managers to monitor vaccination coverage at the district level, identify coverage gaps and missed beneficiaries, and support more effective programme planning and resource allocation.
The national campaign builds on extensive global experience with HPV vaccination.
More than 800 million doses of HPV vaccines have been distributed globally
, providing substantial real-world experience on their use and safety.
HPV vaccination, initially adopted predominantly by high-income countries, has progressively expanded into national immunisation programmes across countries at different income levels. At present,
87 per cent of upper-middle-income countries, 78 per cent of lower-middle-income countries and 54 per cent of low-income countries have adopted HPV vaccines in their National Immunization Programmes
.
The growing adoption of HPV vaccination across diverse income settings reflects its increasing role as an important component of national strategies for cervical cancer prevention.
All vaccination sessions under the campaign are conducted under the supervision of
trained Medical Officers
at Government health facilities.
Government health facilities are also linked with
24×7 healthcare facilities for appropriate management of rare Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI)
. This mechanism ensures timely assessment, monitoring and management of any vaccination-related adverse event.
With the campaign progressing towards its final phase, the focus remains on reaching the remaining eligible beneficiaries and ensuring that
no eligible girl is left behind
.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare continues to work closely with States and Union Territories, healthcare professionals, frontline health workers and communities to strengthen awareness, facilitate access and support effective implementation of the HPV Vaccination Campaign.
The achievement of
80 lakh HPV vaccine doses
marks an important step in India’s efforts to strengthen preventive healthcare and advance long-term protection against cervical cancer among future generations.

title: Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA chairs 9th meeting of CSMC
subtitle: Over 29,000 additional houses approved under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0, total sanctions now at 18.77 Lakh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 10:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has approved a total of 18.77 lakh houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0), giving further impetus to the implementation of scheme and accelerating progress towards ‘Housing for All’ in urban areas. The decision was taken in the 9th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held under the chairmanship of Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA in New Delhi on 10th September 2026.
The meeting was also attended by Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary & Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA), Shri Sanjeet, Joint Secretary & Financial Advisor (JS&FA), senior officials from the Ministry and Mission Directors of from participating States. In today’s meeting over 29,000 houses were approved under Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals of PMAY-U 2.0, covering six States - Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Telangana, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh.
Addressing the States, Secretary, UD (MoHUA), said that concerted efforts towards the timely and effective implementation, monitoring of PMAY-U 2.0 should be ensured so that the benefits of scheme reach all eligible beneficiaries. He further added that any bottlenecks should be promptly identified and addressed in consultation with the States/UTs.
Secretary, UD categorically mentioned that CSMC meetings will be convened every second week of the month to ensure regular monitoring and provide further impetus to the pace of progress of PMAY-U 2.0. He emphasised on States/UTs to submit the duly approved projects by end of each month for their timely consideration and sanction in the subsequent CSMC meetings.
Over 18 lakh families being benefitted
PMAY-U 2.0 seeks to provide housing assistance to eligible urban EWS/LIG and MIG families through its different verticals. Under the scheme, beneficiaries can construct their own pucca house, purchase a house in projects constructed under the scheme, avail affordable rental housing, or benefit from interest subsidy on eligible housing loans, providing a range of housing solutions suited to their needs, eligibility and financial circumstances.
With total 18.77 lakh approved under PMAY-U 2.0, the scheme is steadily expanding access to safe, affordable and pucca homes. These approvals mark a significant step towards ‘Housing for All’, enabling more urban families to move closer to owning a secure home and building a better future.
Major push towards ‘Housing for All’
PMAY-U 2.0 builds on the sustained progress made under PMAY-U. Overall, under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, more than 1.25 crore houses have been sanctioned and over 1 crore houses completed and delivered to beneficiaries.
Housing as a foundation for dignity and empowerment
The scheme caters to the housing needs of EWS/LIG and MIG families, having an annual household income of up to ₹9 lakh, enabling them to transition from kutcha, inadequate or rented accomodation to safe and dignified homes. By enabling vulnerable families to access adequate housing, the scheme has given them a renewed sense of security and stability, while helping them move towards a better quality of life.
The scheme also places strong emphasis on women’s ownership of houses. Houses sanctioned under the scheme are either in the name of woman of the house or in joint ownership, strengthening women’s economic and social position within the household. Of the 18.77 lakh houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0, 17.19 lakh houses (92%) have been allotted to women.
Further, to ensure inclusivity and extend the benefits of the scheme to vulnerable sections of society, 1.80 lakh houses have been allotted to senior citizens. 3.25 lakh houses have been sanctioned for SC beneficiaries, 1.02 lakh for ST beneficiaries and 8.22 lakh for OBC beneficiaries, reaffirming the scheme’s commitment to equitable access to safe, affordable and dignified housing.
With the cumulative number of PMAY-U 2.0 sanctions now approaching the 20-lakh milestone, the Government continues to work towards ensuring that every eligible urban family has a house to call their own. Each house sanctioned represents a family moving closer to a safer, more secure and dignified future.

title: Shram Shakti is Fundamental to National Development: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya

Centre, States and Stakeholders Deliberate on Welfare, Employment, Skilling and Social Security of Construction Workers

State Governments should assess current utilisation of cess funds, identify gaps, and explore new avenues for their effective utilisation, urges Dr. Mandaviya

MoS Shobha Karandlaje Stresses Worker Safety, Social Security and Dignified Working Conditions for Construction Workers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) organised by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, in collaboration with Government of Maharashtra, began in Mumbai today, with Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister of Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, chairing the proceedings.
The conference was attended by the Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Labour Ministers of participating States/UTs, senior officials of the Ministry of Labour & Employment, representatives of State/UT BOCW Welfare Boards, and other stakeholders.
Addressing the conference, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya emphasised that Shram Shakti is integral to the development of a nation and plays a vital role in nation-building. He stated that the social security and welfare of the workforce is therefore fundamental to national development. He stressed the importance of sharing best practices among States and ensuring optimum utilisation of BOCW funds to provide wider social security coverage to workers. He further emphasised the need for the labour ecosystem to continuously evolve with changing times, and underlined the need for the Centre and States to remain aligned in their vision and policies for the holistic welfare of BOCW workers.
The Union Minister also emphasised the need to explore measures that can provide workers with greater dignity, honour and self-respect, including the possibility of providing pension support to workers. He highlighted that the country is undergoing rapid transformation to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047. He further highlighted the growing global demand for skilled and semi-skilled workers, and underscored the need to prepare India’s workforce to meet these emerging opportunities.
Hon’ble Union Minister for Labour & Employment, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, chaired the two-day National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) in Mumbai with Labour Ministers of States and Union Territories. https://t.co/vPRcWQXRPY
— Ministry of Labour & Employment, GoI (@LabourMinistry)
September 11, 2026
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya called for deliberations on international labour mobility, highlighting its significance in the nation’s economic growth through remittances, and in meeting the aspirations of Bharat’s Yuva Shakti. He emphasised upon the need for coordinated efforts by the Centre and States to create a comprehensive platform for international labour mobility, supported by appropriate financial and digital infrastructure, so that Indian workers can access global opportunities while enhancing India’s credibility on the global stage.
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya urged all stakeholders to participate actively in discussions at the two-day conference, with the objective of aligning the outcomes with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat, while empowering Bharat’s Shram Shakti
.
In his address, Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary, Labour & Employment, drew attention to the significance of the Conference, highlighting the number of construction workers across India, which stands at over 7 crores, and the BOCW cess corpus available in the country, amounting to about Rs. 77000 crores. The deliberations at the Conference provide an opportunity to share best practices and engage with industry partners, he said. Noting that the Labour Codes contain several provisions that strengthen social protection and welfare measures for BOCW workers, he said that initiatives alone are not sufficient unless dignity of labour is kept central to the welfare agenda. He underlined the need to develop a holistic welfare model for BOCW workers, taking into account the mobility inherent in their work and ensuring that welfare facilities are designed in a manner that makes them easily accessible to workers wherever their work takes them.
A Compendium of Initiatives for Building and Other Construction Workers was unveiled during the inaugural session, which was followed by presentations on best practices adopted by States/UTs, with Maharashtra presenting its Education Initiative, Haryana its Beneficiary Verification Exercise and Uttarakhand its Health Scheme. The presentations were followed by discussions with participation from the Union Ministers and concerned State representatives.
A key highlight of Day One was the session on three national initiatives aimed at strengthening digital and facilitation mechanisms for construction workers. Presentations were made on the State BOCW Digital Labour Chowk (DLC), Labour Chowk-cum-Facilitation Centres (LCFCs) and Online BOCW Cess Collection Portal. Chhattisgarh gave a detailed presentation on its Digital Labour Chowk, Tamil Nadu on the Labour Chowk-cum-Facilitation Centres and Keralam on the Online BOCW Cess Collection Portal. These three initiatives, as adopted by several participating States, were subsequently launched during the conference.
Several States/UTs, including Maharashtra, Telangana, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Manipur, are taking forward digital and worker-centric initiatives for BOC workers, including the Digital Labour Chowk, which was launched on the occasion. Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Manipur launched Online BOCW Cess Collection Portals and Bihar and West Bengal unveiled Labour Chowk-cum-Facilitation Centres to strengthen access to employment, welfare services and transparent cess management.
The conference also deliberated on International Labour Mobility Pathways, followed by discussions with participating stakeholders. A separate session was held on the construction sector, featuring presentations by Government and industry stakeholders.
In her concluding remarks, the Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Smt. Shobha Karandlaje, emphasised the need for concerted efforts to ensure the registration of all workers and establishments, along with effective utilisation of cess funds. She urged State Governments to strengthen cess collection from construction establishments and ensure the timely and transparent utilisation of accumulated funds for the welfare of workers. She highlighted that BOCW funds could be utilised for key areas such as pension and social security for ageing workers, primary education support for workers’ children, and healthcare coverage.
Sushri Karandlaje further stressed the need for renewed focus on worker safety at construction sites and provision of basic amenities, including toilets and sanitation facilities, creches for children of women workers, and housing support, to ensure dignified working and living conditions for the construction workforce. She appreciated the best practices adopted by various States and emphasised that successful initiatives should be shared and adopted across the country to strengthen the welfare and social security of construction workers.
In his address at the closing of Day 1, Dr. Mandaviya urged State Governments to undertake a detailed assessment of the current utilisation of cess funds, identify gaps, and explore new avenues for their effective utilisation, keeping in view the long-term welfare and social security of workers. He also called upon States to undertake a comprehensive assessment of the impact of the Labour Codes after one year of their implementation and identify areas where more effective execution may be required. He emphasised the need for workshops and orientation programmes for labour law practitioners to facilitate effective implementation of the Codes in letter and spirit.
Highlighting the significance of the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) in promoting employment and expanding social security coverage for new entrants to the workforce, the Union Minister urged State Governments to undertake focused workshops and engagements with industry and other stakeholders. Such efforts, he noted, would help create greater awareness and ensure that eligible new entrants receive the benefits of the scheme, thereby strengthening the collective efforts towards expanding formal employment and worker welfare.
The conference will continue tomorrow with sessions on the roles and responsibilities of BOCW Welfare Boards in the light of the new Labour Codes, skilling and employment, the construction sector and Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW), and Labour Stack.

title: Drylands Must be Reimagined through Resilient Institutions, Digital Public Infrastructure and Community Action: Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 4:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Shri Narendra Bhooshan, emphasised the need to move from responding to droughts after they occur to building resilient dryland landscapes through integrated watershed development, technology and community participation, while speaking at the Dryland Congress 2026 Partner Spotlight at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi, on
“Reimagining Drylands: Institutions, Digital Public Infrastructure and Community Action for a Climate-Resilient Future.”
The Dryland Congress 2026, being held in New Delhi from September 10, has emerged as an important international platform for deliberation on the future of dryland agriculture. The Congress has brought together more than 800 participants from over 25 countries, including scientists, policymakers, development partners, industry representatives, academicians, civil society organisations and farmers, to exchange knowledge and deliberate on science-, technology- and policy-based approaches for building resilient and sustainable dryland agricultural systems.
Shri Bhooshan said that “drylands are not wastelands”, but living and productive landscapes whose potential is constrained by climatic variability. Rainfed agriculture covers about 61.39 million hectares, or 43% of India’s net sown area, and contributes around 40% of the country’s food production.
Highlighting the importance of integrated landscape management, he said, “If we restore the landscape, we restore the water cycle; if we restore the water cycle, we restore livelihoods.” He noted that the watershed approach is particularly relevant to drylands as it integrates land, water, vegetation and livelihoods.
Shri Bhooshan highlighted the contribution of the Watershed Development Component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY), implemented by DoLR. Over the past 12 years, 7,602 watershed development projects covering about 34 million hectares have been implemented. These interventions have created or rejuvenated around 0.9 million water harvesting structures, provided protective irrigation to about 2 million hectares, benefited nearly 6 million farmers, generated 67 million person-days and covered 0.3 million hectares under plantation.
Shri Bhooshan said that watershed development should be viewed as an investment in natural capital, with completed projects demonstrating a Benefit-Cost Ratio of about 2:1 and significant improvements in groundwater, cultivated area, cropping intensity, milk production and farmers’ incomes.
Emphasising technology, he said watershed development must move “from GIS to intelligence—from knowing where an asset exists to knowing whether the landscape is becoming more resilient.” The proposed Watershed Portal will provide an integrated Digital Public Infrastructure covering the lifecycle of watershed projects and incorporating key geospatial datasets.
He stressed that “digital tools can provide the evidence, institutions can provide the framework, and communities provide the ownership.”
Calling for stronger partnerships among governments, research institutions, development partners and communities, Shri Bhooshan said India has an opportunity to develop a scalable Indian Dryland Development Roadmap and demonstrate a global model of landscape restoration and rural prosperity, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
He concluded that the watershed must become “much more than a project boundary”—a platform for restoring natural capital, securing water, strengthening agriculture, creating livelihoods and building climate resilience.

title: Seventh Gender Samvaad emphasises strengthening women’s leadership and agency in livelihoods
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 SEP 2026 9:52AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana– National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), Ministry of Rural Development, in collaboration with the Institute for What Works to Advance Gender Equality (IWWAGE), organized the seventh edition of Gender Samvaad on the theme “Participation to Leadership: Enhancing Women’s Agency in Livelihoods.”
The dialogue witnessed participation from over 6 lakh stakeholders across the country, including SHG women, State Rural Livelihoods Mission staff, policymakers, gender experts, and practitioners, providing a platform for exchange of experiences and to deliberate on strengthening women’s participation, leadership and decision-making in rural livelihoods and economic institutions.
In his keynote address, Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal highlighted the Gender Samvaad’s journey from 1,400 participants in April 2021 to nearly six lakh in September 2025, reflecting the growing voice and leadership. He emphasised the strength of the SHG movement with over 10 crore women being exemplary across the world as a women-led movement. Highlighting state-led innovations, he shared about Maharashtra’s Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill recognising women farmers without formal land titles, Odisha’s Bhubaneswar Declaration advancing women’s land rights and representation in agricultural institutions, and Andhra Pradesh’s RySS natural farming model, driven at scale by women’s SHGs.
He also highlighted that over 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis earning more than ₹1 lakh annually is equally strengthening women’s economic aspirations. He underscored the need to identify, adapt and scale such innovations across States and strengthen women’s role as producers, entrepreneurs, decision-makers and leaders in building a Viksit Bharat.
Welcoming the participants, Joint Secretary-RL, Ministry of Rural Development, Shri Amit Shukla highlighted the evolution of gender integration under DAY-NRLM- from mobilisation to institutionalising gender as a mainstream concern in programme design and implementation. He noted that initiatives such as the Gender Advisory issued in December 2021, Nayi Chetna as the Annual National Gender Campaign, the Gender Integration Workshop, and the Practice Guide for Gender Integration in Livelihoods have progressively strengthened this approach. Emphasising the next frontier of women’s collective economic institutions, including CLFs, Producer Groups, Producer Enterprises and FPOs, he called for stronger governance and managerial capacities, financial record-keeping and credit-readiness, particularly in the context of the UN International Year of Women Farmers 2026.
Smt. Swati Sharma, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, highlighted the ongoing National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II (21 August–21 November 2026) as an important step towards strengthening entrepreneurship among SHG women through enterprise development, value chains, digital platforms and market access. She emphasised that collectivisation through SHGs, federations, Producer Groups, FPOs/FPCs and Producer Enterprises, supported by financial inclusion, skills, technology, market linkages and asset ownership, is critical to strengthening women’s economic agency and leadership. She called for a whole-of-government and convergence approach, bringing together Ministries and Departments, technical and research institutions, academia, civil society and development partners to mainstream gender across livelihood and entrepreneurship initiatives.
Other speakers enriched the dialogue with diverse insights and approaches. Smt. Garima Sai Sundaram, SPM–Non-Farm Livelihoods, Madhya Pradesh, highlighted how economic empowerment and access to resources strengthen women’s bargaining power and sustain their leadership. Smt. Seema Kulkarni, MAKAAM, emphasised the need for social protection and support systems to enable women’s participation and leadership. Prof. Nitya Rao, Gender and Livelihoods Expert, underscored convergence, institutional support, addressing unpaid care work and gaps in resource ownership, and access to appropriate tools and technologies to strengthen women’s economic identity, representation and sustainable leadership.
Women leaders from Assam and Maharashtra shared their journeys from SHG membership to entrepreneurship, leadership and decision-making. Smt. Niharika Bhuyan from Sonitpur, Assam, progressed from an SHG member to a leader in a women-led FPC, highlighting how collective action, training and institutional support enabled women farmers to strengthen their economic participation and decision-making. Smt. Kirti Tai Deshmukh from Akola, Maharashtra, moved from being a homemaker to an entrepreneur, demonstrating how SHG-based training and access to government schemes helped her establish her enterprise, build confidence and inspire other women to pursue entrepreneurship.
The Seventh Gender Samvaad, aligned with the UN International Year of Women Farmers 2026, provided a national platform to recognise and amplify the contributions of women farmers and their livelihood institutions to rural livelihoods, food systems and local economies. Launched in April 2021 as a joint initiative of DAY-NRLM and IWWAGE, Gender Samvaad has evolved into a national platform for knowledge exchange and policy dialogue, reaffirming gender equality as a key driver of women’s economic empowerment and inclusive rural development.

title: Critical Minerals Key to India’s Energy Security, Industrial Competitiveness and National Security: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Dr Jitendra Singh Says India Moves from Technology Follower to Confident Global Player; Calls for Stronger Industry-Research Partnerships and Domestic Capabilities

Dr Jitendra Singh Says India Must Combine Domestic Resources with Global Partnerships to Build Resilient Value Chains

Dr Jitendra Singh Calls for Whole-of-Nation Approach to Secure India’s Strategic Materials and Technology Future

date:
